title: PainCard
description: Standardized schema for atomic pain point cards extracted from organic developer and user conversations (Reddit, HN, X, GitHub, App Store, Discord).

id.description: Globally unique identifier for the pain card. Recommended format: pain-YYYYMMDD-<slug>.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this card was extracted or recorded.

headline.description: One-line punchy summary of the specific pain point (under 100 characters).

target_audience.description: Detailed profile of who suffers from this pain point.

role.description: Specific job title, persona, or identity (e.g. Solo SaaS Founder, Junior DevOps Engineer, Shopify Merchant).

domain.description: Industry or functional vertical (e.g. Developer Tools, E-commerce, B2B Sales, Creative / Design).

experience_or_scale.description: Scale indicator (e.g. 1-5 person team, $10k-50k MRR, hobbyist, high-volume production).

scenario.description: The exact context, workflow step, or trigger event where the user encounters the friction.

friction.description: The specific breakdown, failure, bottleneck, or obstruction preventing the user from completing their objective.

current_workaround.description: How the user currently hacks around the problem in the absence of a dedicated solution.

method.description: Description of the manual workaround, DIY script, or operational duct tape.

tools_used.description: List of existing tools stitched together to cope with the problem.

drawbacks.description: Why this workaround is inadequate, fragile, tedious, or dangerous.

cost_or_loss.description: Quantified or qualitative estimate of what the pain costs the user or business.

summary.description: Concise summary of total financial, operational, or emotional damage.

time_lost_hours_per_month.description: Estimated hours wasted every month dealing with this pain.

financial_loss_usd_per_month.description: Direct financial cost, wasted ad spend, cloud bill spike, or contractor fee.

emotional_toll.description: Emotional severity reported or inferred from user language.

sentiment_intensity.description: Aggregate level of urgency and desperation expressed by the user.

paying_intent_clues.description: Concrete signals that the user or their organization would pay to eradicate this pain.

has_explicit_buying_statement.description: True if user stated things like 'I would pay $X', 'Shut up and take my money', 'Looking for a paid tool'.

existing_spend_on_workaround.description: True if user already pays for human freelancers, Zapier runs, or clunky enterprise software to patch this.

stated_budget_range.description: Reported willingness to pay (e.g. '$20-$50/month', '$500 one-time', 'seat-based enterprise budget').

evidence_snippets.description: Direct quote segments demonstrating willingness to pay or acute economic loss.

source_url.description: Direct canonical link to the public post, thread, review, or issue.

channel.description: Platform or origin channel where this signal was harvested.

channel_metadata.description: Source-specific metadata (e.g., subreddit, upvotes, thread author, engagement).

raw_quote.description: Verbatim quote of the user's original words with no rewriting or AI embellishment.

confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0 to 1.0) assessing extraction accuracy and authenticity (filters out stealth spam/marketing).

tags.description: Keywords for indexing, search, and clustering.

cluster_id.description: Identifier of the clustered opportunity group this pain card belongs to.
